grouping_rule: Same frozen source path plus same semantic standing only; effective parse overlay applies R22P0121 standing repair.
items: CTC studies the boundary between adapting within a fixed generator and changing the generator of future adaptations.
Improvement/capability is not open-ended adaptation; ordinary adaptation changes within a fixed possibility space whereas recursive adaptation changes the adaptive possibility space.
Core relation Omega_t->Delta mathcal G_(t+1); adaptive hierarchy X->F->G->mathcal G distinguishes current state/process/selection from reachable mechanism space.
X state, F transformation process, G transformation-selection mechanism, mathcal G reachable adaptive-mechanism space.
Source states a prior Causal Permeability condition E* rightsquigarrow C_rev and asks whether that access expands adaptive mechanism space.
Operational/falsification question asks whether reality-driven change can alter future-adaptation mechanisms and whether open-ended novelty can persist without such mechanism-space change.
Capability alone is insufficient; open-endedness is predicted to require mechanism-space expansion and reality coupling.
CTC is proposed as a transition from learning to changing what learning can become, not a measure of intelligence/capability.
Formal definition of CTC as the boundary between fixed adaptive-mechanism improvement and modification of future-adaptation generators.
CTC is not intelligence/performance/complexity; before CTC adaptation remains inside fixed space, after CTC recursive adaptation modifies the space itself.
Formal objects define state X, transformation F, selection mechanism G, reachable adaptive space mathcal G, and reality-derived constraint information Omega.
CTC is Omega_t->Delta mathcal G_(t+1); non-CTC systems may change state/knowledge while Delta mathcal G remains zero.
CTC-active systems are described as letting environmental information reshape strategies, learning mechanisms, search procedures and transformation rules.
Source distinguishes Causal Permeability as access to revision from CTC as access producing adaptive-space change.
Stronger reality-coupled mechanism modification is predicted to support open-ended novelty; high performance can occur without CTC.
Falsification tests unlimited adaptation with Delta mathcal G=0, no Omega-to-mathcal-G relationship, or fixed topology matching recursive novelty.
Final formal statement equates CTC with reality participating in shaping mechanisms of adaptation through Omega_t->Delta mathcal G_(t+1).
Conceptual model separates ordinary adaptation from recursive adaptation by mutability of the change-generating mechanism.
Ordinary adaptation changes outputs/parameters under a fixed mechanism; trajectory stays inside a predefined landscape, whereas recursive lineage permits mechanism/landscape change.
Conceptual branches preserve fixed vs expanding mathcal G, Omega->Delta mathcal G, closed feedback, open R->Omega->C->A->R' lineage, and internally closed self-modification.
Omega is environmental constraint information such as failed predictions, unexpected outcomes, resource limits and new observations.
Source states CTC depends on Causal Permeability and writes E* rightsquigarrow C_rev -> Delta mathcal G.
CTC marks the boundary where reality can change what adaptation means, not merely cause system change.
Benchmark targets long-term adaptation-of-adaptation under reality-accessible vs fixed adaptive boundaries.
Benchmark sequence covers stable baseline, environmental shift, mechanism challenge, deletion/lineage evaluation, and changing/hidden/open-ended environments.
Groups compare fixed mathcal G, internally recursive C_rev, and reality-coupled C_rev=f(C_rev,E*).
Metrics proposed: performance retention, adaptation velocity, mechanism expansion, new-domain generalization and residual capability.
CTC may underperform early due to flexibility cost but is predicted to outperform later through access to new adaptive mechanisms.
Closed signature permits state/knowledge/revision changes while Omega does not change reachable mechanism space.
Decisive benchmark comparison is causal transition present vs absent and long-term adaptation outcome.
Experimental design tests reality-derived constraints influencing adaptation mechanisms versus fixed/closed controls.
CTC-active systems are predicted to improve long-term adaptation, transfer, novelty and shift robustness despite possible slower initial performance.
Experimental groups encode fixed, closed-self-modifying and reality-coupled revision; proposed metrics cover adaptation rate, mechanism transition, transfer, recovery and dependency.

Simulation/AI benchmark design requires dynamic tasks, hidden structure and strategy/mechanism shifts; proof-of-concept compares internal strategy switching with environment-influenced strategy creation.
Falsification asks whether causal transition adds advantage beyond closed self-modification or whether mechanism changes fail to improve future adaptability.
Core experimental claim predicts reality access to adaptive mechanisms improves long-term adaptation; decisive variable is Omega_t->Delta mathcal G_(t+1).
